answer: Running 105 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the relic schedule in the opal ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the beacon checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 3 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
